pr_body:
Fix #3748 by applying the following changes:
 - Add a new autoScaling property to the dialog's canvas so we can scale mouse positions and the surface used to draw its content.
 - Update app.script.Theme to hold the current ui scaling and take charge of calculating the styleMetrics and returning the dimensions downscaled by the ui scaling factor, so it will return the same value independently of the ui scaling. 
 - Add a new m_uiscale member to GraphicsContext to hold the current ui::guiscale() and use it to automatically scale drawing/measuring operations as needed.
pr_comments:

Sure, I think it would be definitively better if the memory overhead is negligible. At least it should be better than the CPU overhead I guess.
I have pushed the suggested changes. Hope the bigger changes are close to what you had in mind.

issue_context.title: UI Elements Scaling doesn't apply to the canvas
issue_context.body:
The Preferences option `UI Element Scaling` doesn't apply to the canvas, leaving it to the script developer to multiply all values/sizes by the scaling value. Without it, elements drawn on the canvas will be misaligned after changing the scale of UI elements.

### Aseprite and System version

* Aseprite version: 1.3-rc1-x64, Steam
* System: Windows/macOS/Linux, version, distribution
comments:
Hi @thkwznk! Thinking about this and you are right, probably to simplify the user side, the canvas could be scaled by default with the UI Scaling, but a flag could be provided for `Dialog:canvas{}` to disable the ui scaling (so all screen pixels are available for the canvas if the script takes care of it).

Also the UI scale is not easily accessible (only under `app.preferences.general.ui_scale`, probably we can add `app.uiScale`)
